$comment:
This repository's own plugin catalogue, hosted in the tree rather than anywhere else, so a session gets its plugins from the same commit as the code they act on — nothing to publish, nothing to keep in sync, and a change to a plugin is reviewed in the pull request that makes it.

`.claude/settings.json` registers this directory in `extraKnownMarketplaces` and enables the plugin, so a developer runs no command in the normal case. Both keys ARE honoured at project scope — measured against Claude Code 2.1.223, and the earlier note here claiming `extraKnownMarketplaces` is skipped in project settings was measured against 2.1.222 and is no longer true. The safety property it described has not gone away, it moved: project-scope registration is read only after the trust dialog for this directory is accepted, so the checkout still cannot fetch plugin code its owner never agreed to — the gate is the trust prompt rather than a skipped key. The `directory` path is relative and resolves against the project root; `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` is NOT expanded there and aborts session startup, so do not reach for it.

Enabling a plugin does not install it. A first session prints `Plugin "<name>@<market>" is enabled in project settings but isn't installed — run `claude plugin install <name>@<market> --scope project``, and that one command is the only manual step. It writes to the user's plugin cache, never into this tree.

Claude Code ignores manifest keys it does not know (`claude plugin validate` says so in as many words), which is where this note lives; the same convention as `coverage.config.json` at the repo root.
